title: deferred-eviction-safety-buffer-and-predictive-cohort-scaling
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Dedicated pools occasionally experience short-duration spikes where preemptive node eviction causes oscillation and SLA violations. This PR introduces a deferred-eviction safety buffer paired with a predictive cohort-scaling signal to reduce churn while keeping throughput guarantees intact.

Summary: Implement a cohort-based credit window that defers non-critical evictions for a short, bounded interval when a tenant's ephemeral burst is detected. Meanwhile, a lightweight predictive estimator (cohort scaler) monitors cohort-level short-term rate-of-arrival and triggers proactive cohort scale-up when sustained utilization is likely. The design prioritizes predictability: eviction deferral is bounded, credits decay deterministically, and we prefer scaling over eviction when cost/latency budget allows.

Key behaviors: 1) Each tenant in a dedicated fleet is assigned a cohort_id (cohort grouping is configurable by tenant tag). 2) When eviction pressure would normally remove warmlets, the eviction controller consults the cohort credit store; if credits exist, eviction is deferred and credits are consumed. 3) Credits are minted when burst mitigation budget is available, and decayed on a fixed half-life to avoid long-term accumulation. 4) A predictive cohort scaler uses short-window exponential smoothing over request arrival to decide on a proactive scale-up; it emits a scale recommendation instead of forcing immediate provisioning, enabling controlled rollouts by the autoscaler.

Files: See changed files for implementation + tests + docs. The RFC contains configuration knobs and migration guidance.

Backward compatibility / migration: Defaults preserve current behavior (credits disabled). Operators can enable cohort grouping and configure default credit windows in the dedicated helm chart. No data migration required; the cohort credit store is schemaless and backed by existing etcd-backed controller state.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator logic and credit decay, integration test that simulates ephemeral spike and verifies reduced eviction churn, e2e smoke verifying no regression to throughput SLO under normal load. CI initially failed one flaky test related to timing; fixed by replacing wall-clock sleeps with injected clock in tests.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated off by default. 2) Enable in canary pools for 48h with detailed metrics. 3) If no regressions, enable for non-critical tenants, then expand cohort coverage. 4) Monitor new metrics and runbook (added) for when deferred-evictions exceed threshold.

Related: ENG-2105 (work item), SUP-4221 (customer request for reduced churn during bursts).

review_conversation: Arjun Patel (review): Overall looks good, but we need to be careful about metric cardinality for cohort_id. If cohorts are per-tenant we could explode Prometheus series. Consider sampling or hashing and provide high-cardinality knobs.

Maya Thompson (author): Agreed. Updated eviction_metrics.go to emit cohort histogram buckets and a sampled tag (cohort_bucket) instead of raw tenant id. Added docs on recommended cardinality sizing and a flag to cap cohorts emitted to metrics.
Lin Zhao (review): The predictive scaler could introduce false positives during noise. Did you validate the smoothing window choices?

Maya Thompson (author): Added unit tests over multiple arrival scenarios and included a canary config in values.yaml that uses conservative thresholds. We also expose smoothing alpha as an operator-configurable knob.
Samir Kapoor (approval): Verified e2e smoke on canary pool; observed ~62% fewer eviction events during ephemeral spikes in test runs. Approving pending CI green.
CI (system): One flaky test timed out (cohort_allocator_test.go:TestCreditDecay) on first run. Replaced time.Sleep with injected clock and re-ran CI - all checks passed.
Merge coach (bot): Squash-merge approved; please ensure release notes entry is present.
release_notes: Introduce deferred-eviction safety buffer and predictive cohort scaling: feature gated for Dedicated. Reduces eviction-induced churn during ephemeral bursts and adds new observability for cohort-level utilization. See docs/rfc for configuration and rollout steps.
